source.title: Optimizer Benchmarking Needs to Account for Hyperparameter Tuning
source.authors: Prabhu Teja Sivaprasad; Florian Mai; Thijs Vogels; Martin Jaggi; François Fleuret

record.file_problem: Text includes the paper and appendix; no apparent truncation affecting the reported experiments.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares optimizers using automatic hyperparameter search budgets and held-out performance, bearing on V4 with a different tuning protocol than the version’s limited-tuning comparisons.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out performance by optimizer and search budget, so these results bear on V4. Claims about prior studies in the related-work section are not extracted as this paper's results. The study does not test the other versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out performance of Adam and SGD variants under automatic random-search budgets, testing V4 with a different tuning protocol. It is not an original source of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that Adam with only its learning rate tuned is particularly practical under limited automatic search budgets. Additional tuning becomes more useful as budgets grow, while SGD can achieve the best performance in some settings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses random search over calibrated, dataset-independent hyperparameter priors, with performance aggregated over search budgets; the claim's cited comparisons focus on limited learning-rate and decay-schedule tuning. Reports test-set performance.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with tuning budget, task, and which hyperparameters are tuned; Adam's first quartile remains lower than Adam-LR's even at the largest budgets. Appendix H reports that SGD-LReff improves low-budget SGD results but performs increasingly worse than SGD-MW at large budgets.

fits_no_version.finding: Tuning additional Adam hyperparameters often hurts at small search budgets and can help at larger budgets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of tuning additional optimizer hyperparameters depends on the search budget and task.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam-LR has the largest displayed probability of winning across the pooled benchmark.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer selection probabilities depend on the search budget and hyperparameter priors.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (Proceedings of the 37th ICML, PMLR 119, 2020)
record.problems: The study says it does not evaluate Bayesian HPO because of computational cost, assumes independently sampled hyperparameters, and does not model complex parameter relationships in its main protocol. Some plot values are not stated numerically in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Other task-level CPE entries in Appendix E.1 Table 6 and per-task/per-budget optimizer comparisons in Figures 4–6 and 9 are not separately rowed; the retained rows cover the text-described budget trends, the aggregate comparison, and distinct Table 6 task outcomes, within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected architectural comparisons.

Matched training-performance comparisons, Adam-to-SGD switching, decoupled weight decay, and the specific word-level language-model qualification. IMDB is sentiment classification; the language-generation task is character-level. The protocol also does not reproduce the original dataset-specific learning-rate and schedule searches.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-scaled weight sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence.

missing.what: The pooled optimizer ranking remains similar when budget is measured by simulated computation time rather than configuration count.
missing.versions: V4; robustness of the pooled comparison, with the same mixed-task scope limitation.

missing.what: CIFAR-10 learning-rate surfaces have similar widths, but SGD-MC WC has a slightly higher optimum and better high-budget performance than Adam-LR.
missing.versions: V4; supports the CIFAR-10 disadvantage for Adam-LR at high search budgets.

missing.what: Accounting for effective learning rate improves low-budget SGD-MW performance, but the pooled SGD variants still trail Adam-LR across budgets.
missing.locator: Appendix H, Figure 10 and accompanying text
missing.versions: V4; sensitivity to the search parameterization, subject to the pooled-task limitation.

record.verdict_notes: The study's held-out comparisons test V4 despite its focus on tuning effort. Within-Adam comparisons do not independently test V4. Search priors are calibrated across tasks and their calibration cost is excluded; training uses validation-based stopping. No supplied training-performance comparison establishes whether held-out differences persist at equal training fit. Other table entries and per-budget comparisons explicitly declared in rows_left_out are not repeated as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Width beyond interpolation and test error.
Language benchmarks are represented only by the study's IMDB LSTM task; the study does not compare decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD.

rows.subject: Adam-LR
rows.operation_detail: Random-search hyperparameter configurations; report test accuracy after budgets 1, 4, 16, and 64.
rows.value: Figure 4 plots the values; exact values not stated in text.
rows.uncertainty: First and second quartiles are shown in Figure 4; exact uncertainty values not stated in text.
rows.note: Authors state Adam-LR and the fixed-parameter SGD counterpart outperform their more-parameterized counterparts on all classification tasks through budget 16.
rows.check: Adam-LR versus Adam measures tuning within one optimizer family, not adaptive versus SGD performance. The text establishes the advantage through budget 16; the supplied figure text cannot establish the CIFAR-10 comparison at budget 64.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Random-search hyperparameter configurations with all Adam parameters tuned; report test accuracy after budgets 1, 4, 16, and 64.
rows.value: Figure 4 plots the values; exact values not stated in text.
rows.uncertainty: First and second quartiles are shown in Figure 4; exact uncertainty values not stated in text.
rows.note: At higher budgets Adam can outperform Adam-LR on some classification tasks; the first quartile remains far lower than Adam-LR's, including at the largest budgets.
rows.check: The comparison is Adam versus Adam-LR. The stated high-budget improvements concern CIFAR-100, FMNIST and IMDB, not explicitly CIFAR-10.

rows.subject: Adam-LR
rows.operation_detail: Random-search hyperparameter configurations; aggregate relative performance across tasks as budget increases.
rows.measure: Aggregated relative performance to the best optimizer per task
rows.baseline: Best optimizer performance per task at that budget
rows.value: Adam-LR performs very close to the best optimizer for all budgets; exact values not stated in text.
rows.note: The text describes the aggregate curve; no exact numeric values are given for Adam-LR.
rows.check: Together with R4, the aggregate favors Adam-LR over SGD. However, the nine-task pool also contains VAEs and an artificial quadratic problem; it does not establish an image- or language-only effect.

rows.subject: SGD-MC WC
rows.operation_detail: Random-search hyperparameter configurations; aggregate relative performance across tasks as budget increases.
rows.measure: Aggregated relative performance to the best optimizer per task
rows.value: SGD variants perform 20% worse in early HPO; the gap narrows to 10% as tuning budgets increase.
rows.note: SGD-MC WC is one of the SGD variants contributing to the aggregate SGD comparison; the text does not provide its separate aggregate values.
rows.check: The 20% and 10% shortfalls describe the pooled SGD variants, not separate numerical estimates for SGD-MC WC. They are relative aggregate-performance differences, not accuracy percentage points.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Random-search hyperparameter configurations; compare aggregate performance to Adam-LR over increasing budgets.
rows.measure: Aggregated relative performance gap to Adam-LR
rows.value: Adam leaves a 2–3% gap at high budgets.
rows.note: Adam improves steadily relative to Adam-LR, but still has a 2–3% gap at high budgets.
rows.check: The 2–3% gap compares fully tuned Adam with Adam-LR, not Adam with SGD.

rows.subject: Adam-LR
rows.operation_detail: Random-search hyperparameter configurations; compute probability of being the best optimizer across tasks at each search budget.

conditions.value: search budgets up to 60 models trained

rows.value: 58% (only learning rate tuned), as shown in Figure 1.
rows.note: Figure 1 gives 58% for Adam with only learning rate tuned; Adam with all parameters tuned is 17%, SGD with tuned learning rate and fixed momentum and weight decay is 13%, and SGD with tuned learning-rate schedule and fixed momentum and weight decay is 12%.
rows.check: Probability of winning is a selection statistic rather than the magnitude of held-out performance. The displayed 58% is not established as a constant across budgets.

rows.subject: Adam-LR
rows.operation_detail: Compute cumulative performance-early aggregation of incumbent performance across the full tuning sequence.
rows.note: Table reports CPE as a task-level aggregate.
rows.check: The value 91.6% is correct, but its recorded comparator is Adam. This within-Adam comparison does not establish V4.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Compute cumulative performance-early aggregation of incumbent performance across the full tuning sequence.
rows.note: At this aggregation, Adam's result is slightly below Adam-LR.
rows.check: The value 91.3% is correct, but its recorded comparator is Adam-LR. The small difference does not measure an adaptive-versus-SGD disadvantage.

rows.subject: SGD-MC WC
rows.operation_detail: Compute cumulative performance-early aggregation of incumbent performance across the full tuning sequence.
rows.note: SGD-MC WC has higher CPE than Adam-LR on this task; Adam-LR is 78.8%.
rows.check: Correct: CIFAR-10 CPE is 81.0% for SGD-MC WC versus 78.8% for Adam-LR. CPE averages incumbent test accuracies with greater weight on earlier search budgets.

rows.subject: SGD-MC D
rows.operation_detail: Compute cumulative performance-early aggregation of incumbent performance across the full tuning sequence.
rows.note: This optimizer is also reported to exceed Adam-LR on CIFAR 10; Adam-LR is 78.8%.
rows.check: Correct: CIFAR-10 CPE is 82.1% for SGD-MC D versus 78.8% for Adam-LR; this SGD variant also tunes the learning-rate decay exponent.

rows.subject: SGD-MC WC
rows.operation_detail: Compute cumulative performance-early aggregation of incumbent performance across the full tuning sequence.
rows.note: Tie with Adam-LR, which is also 95.3%.
rows.check: Both methods have reported CPE of 95.3% on the SVHN wide residual network, so the reported measure shows no adaptive-method disadvantage.

rows.subject: SGD-MW
rows.operation_detail: Compute cumulative performance-early aggregation of incumbent performance across the full tuning sequence.
rows.note: Table reports competing optimizer performance; Adam-LR is 42.0%.
rows.check: SGD-MW reaches 33.2% versus Adam-LR's 42.0% on CIFAR-100. This clearly favors Adam-LR, rather than showing a partial adaptive-method disadvantage.

rows.subject: Adam-WC D
rows.operation_detail: Compute cumulative performance-early aggregation of incumbent performance across the full tuning sequence.
rows.note: Adam-LR is 85.9%; Table 6 shows Adam-WC D, a distinct optimizer configuration.
rows.check: The 86.0% value is correct, but the comparison is between Adam configurations. Table 4 defines Adam-WC D as Adam-LR plus a tuned Poly decay schedule; this is not an AdamW experiment.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Compare Adam with all hyperparameters tuned against Adam-LR across budgets.
rows.value: Adam outperforms Adam-LR on IMDB at higher budgets; exact values not stated in text.
rows.note: Text states Adam outperforms Adam-LR on IMDB at higher budgets.
rows.check: The text supports the high-budget improvement, but Adam versus Adam-LR does not establish adaptive-versus-SGD performance.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, early-weighted cumulative performance under calibrated random search
relationships.reason: SGD variants exceed Adam-LR's 78.8% CPE, reaching 81.0% and 82.1% (R9, R10).
relationships.display_finding: Reported early-weighted cumulative performance favors SGD variants over Adam-LR, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100, Adam-LR versus SGD-MW under early-weighted cumulative performance
relationships.reason: Adam-LR reaches 42.0% CPE versus SGD-MW's 33.2%, reversing the adaptive-method disadvantage (R12).
relationships.display_finding: Adam-LR reportedly achieved higher early-weighted cumulative performance than SGD-MW, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: SVHN wide residual network, Adam-LR versus SGD-MC WC under cumulative performance
relationships.reason: Both methods report 95.3% CPE, showing no adaptive-method disadvantage at the reported precision (R11).
relationships.display_finding: Adam-LR and SGD-MC WC reportedly tied at the reported precision, but this cumulative-performance comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Pooled nine-task benchmark with dataset-independent calibrated search priors
relationships.reason: The pooled SGD variants trail Adam-LR by approximately 20% early and 10% later; this qualifies the optimizer ranking by search protocol, although the pool includes tasks outside V4 (R3, R4).
relationships.display_finding: Pooled results for SGD variants reportedly trailed Adam-LR when hyperparameter searches used calibrated probabilities to sample settings. The comparison remains unverified and includes tasks beyond image and language benchmarks.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Automatic hyperparameter search across the study's nine tasks and tested budgets
reader_labels.reason: Adam-LR is usually the safest low-budget choice and remains competitive, but fully tuned Adam improves at higher budgets and can outperform Adam-LR on some tasks; SGD variants also win in some task/aggregation settings (R1–R14).
